pr.title: ci: pin lint environment to Python 3.11
pr.body:
### Description

The lint workflow currently selects CPython 3.15.1 through `python-version: '3.x'`. Installing the frozen dependencies then builds SciPy 1.16.3 from source and fails because OpenBLAS is unavailable, before the formatting checks run.

Use Python 3.11 in both setup-python and uv sync, matching the existing unit-test workflow. This changes two lines in one workflow. The lock file, dependency versions, and isort, black and flake8 commands are unchanged.

### Related issues or pull requests

Observed on #1267, #1268 and #1269. Their unit-test workflows pass with Python 3.11; their lint jobs fail during dependency installation:
- [#1267 lint job](https://github.com/rasbt/mlxtend/actions/runs/41035116094/job/123993938948)
- [#1268 lint job](https://github.com/rasbt/mlxtend/actions/runs/41035417587/job/123994929556)
- [#1269 lint job](https://github.com/rasbt/mlxtend/actions/runs/41035609504/job/123995568470)

### Verification

Hosted validation on commit `410abc2b778310c64cab57dd284171a73747181d` in the fork succeeded:
- [Lint workflow](https://github.com/Afloat16/mlxtend/actions/runs/41763206302): dependency installation and all existing lint commands passed.
- [Unit-test workflow](https://github.com/Afloat16/mlxtend/actions/runs/41763206340): both build-linux and build-linux-latest-sklearn passed.

The validation PR is based on the same upstream master commit `1aee767ef57b84a8191511a08955c583b65de382`. The upstream PR still needs its own required checks.

This is a CI configuration change, so product documentation, a release note and new product unit tests are not applicable.

independentReview716.scope: Independent static review of response metadata, semantic header comparison and same-request 304 replacement at capacity. No remote mutation or runtime test execution.
independentReview716.conclusion: No remaining semantic blocker identified in this reviewed version. Current-head CI stopped at formatting; runtime validation remains pending.

issues: Header name case and cross-name order should not create distinct samples; preserve value order within one name.
Unavailable 304 samples must not prevent a later usable same-request answer at the route cap while preserving missing evidence for other requests.

verified_invariants: same_sample exhaustively destructures Sample and compares every field; original stored headers and public serialized equality are unchanged.

same_headers ignores ASCII name case and order between names, preserving per-name value order and multiplicity. Equal total lengths plus matching named sequences excludes extra unmatched right-hand names.

At full capacity only an unavailable status-304 sample with identical sanitized path, query and request key is eligible for replacement. Hidden request keys use the same helper in selection and construction.

A missing cached body or any explicitly refused body (except existing NotRecorded empty-response semantics) does not evict the unavailable sample. Current make_sample refusal paths have not charged body bytes.

An actual repeat refunds only the newly charged body and never removes the 304. A distinct usable replacement removes the earliest eligible entry, increments the omitted count and appends in recording order.
Query/resource/GraphQL-operation evidence prevents fallback to unrelated recorded responses. Rejected bodies do not double-count scrubbed headers.
The original five metadata regressions are byte-for-byte unchanged.

With cap=2, total=2, entries [unavailable304, 200:'ok', repeated200:'ok'], make_sample rejected the third body as FileLimit but left status200. The candidate would evict the 304 and store an empty200, changing replay.
found_and_fixed_before_publication.resolution: Replacement guard also refuses any body_left_out other than NotRecorded. Budget-2/4 controls distinguish early rejection from a real charged-then-refunded repeat.

meaningful_negative_controls: different query, numeric resource and GraphQL operation
